quotes.quote: Lists vulnerabilities for given package and version. May also be queried by commit hash.
commit string The commit hash to query for. If specified, version should not be set.
A fuzzy match is done against upstream versions.
If set, commit must not be used, and package.purl must not include a version.
When a commit hash is given, this is optional.
If your previous query fetched a large number of results, the response will be paginated.
Use either the top-level version field or a versioned purl (pkg:...@<version>), but not both.
Requests that specify the version in both places return 400 Bad Request.
Invalid (400 Bad Request):
{ "package": { "purl": "pkg:pypi/jinja2@3.1.4" }, "version": "3.1.4" }
{ "package": { "purl": "pkg:pypi/jinja2" }, "version": "3.1.4" }
Case Sensitivity: API requests are case-sensitive.
Package names are matched exactly, except in ecosystems whose registry treats other spellings as the same package:
PyPI names are normalized as described in PEP 503,
NuGet names are matched case-insensitively,
crates.io names are matched case-insensitively with
To do so, set the ecosystem to GIT, enter the full URL of the repository to the name field,
and the tag into the version field.
{"package": {"name": "https://github.com/curl/curl.git", "ecosystem": "GIT"}, "version": "8.5.0"}
"commit": "string",
"page_token": "string"
pagination will occur when there more than 1,000 vulnerabilities in the response, or when the query has exceeded 20 seconds.
When pagination is used, the next_page_token is given in the response, indicating that there are more results to return.
repeating queries until the next_page_token is no longer included in the response.
To get the next page of results, your next request must include page_token:
In rare cases, the response might contain only the next_page_token.
please keep querying with the next_page_token until either results are returned, or no more page tokens are returned.
The API has a response size limit of 32MiB when using HTTP/1.1.
There is no limit when using HTTP/2.
We recommend using HTTP/2 for queries that may result in large responses.
The page size can vary slightly because of threading and may change in the future.
